editorial:
Imagine meeting the perfect guy. He is polite, handy around the house, and treats everyone with total kindness. That is exactly how Henry Morrison looks to the world. But here is the scary part: he is actually a killer who wipes out his family whenever they stop being perfect. You get to follow him as he moves to a new town, changes his name, and tries to trick a lonely widow and her daughter into loving him. The vibe is super tense because you know he is a monster, but the people around him have no clue. It makes you feel uneasy every time he smiles.

Terry Ferrone does an amazing job playing the lead because he can switch from sweet to scary in a split second. The movie moves quickly and does not waste your time with boring scenes. While some of the 80s effects look a bit dated, the suspense still works great today. If you like stories about people hiding dark secrets, you will love this one.
endingExplained: The movie ends with a big fight between Henry and the daughter, Stephanie. She figures out his secret and tries to stop him. After a scary chase, Henry is finally beaten and killed. However, the very last scene shows a new man meeting a woman. He looks and acts just like Henry did at the start. This means the cycle is starting all over again with a different killer looking for a new family.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves psychological thrillers and creepy villains.
